transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, thank you for agreeing to speak with me. I wanted to come by and talk to you about the blood transfusion you received during your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, I'm just so tired. My Arthur always told me I was too frail for these things. He would have been right here holding my hand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling very exhausted. I have something important to tell you. There was a mistake in how we handled your blood type verification before the operation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean? Was I given the wrong thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some issues with the process and things didn't go quite right with the verification steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Is my blood contaminated? Is that why I feel so shaky? I can't believe this. Arthur would be so worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be very clear. I am deeply sorry. I am responsible for this error and I take full accountability for the fact that we did not follow the correct protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I can't lose anyone else. I'm all alone in this big room and now you're telling me something went wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's very difficult to hear this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what actually happened? You said there was a mistake. Who did it? Why did it happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the pre-operative checks and we didn't verify the type as we should have. But the blood you received was compatible, so you are safe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Compatible? But if it was a mistake, then it wasn't the right one, was it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a compatible type, just not the ideal match for your specific blood group.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm drifting. My husband always handled the doctors. He knew how to ask the right questions. I don't know what to ask.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is overwhelming.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did this make the surgery worse? Am I going to have a reaction now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are stable. I am truly sorry for this failure. It was my responsibility to ensure those checks were done, and I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just keep thinking about how he'd be so angry. He hated it when people were careless.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, what now? Do I need more blood? Do I need a different kind of medicine to fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to keep a close eye on your labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Like, today? Or tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will check your blood levels over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's it? Just checking? I don't feel right. I feel like something is off in my chest.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I believe that's the recovery from the anesthesia.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't telling me what actually happened. You keep saying "confusion" and "process." I want to know exactly what went into my arm.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were steps in the verification process that were skipped.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which steps? Who skipped them? Was it you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am the one responsible for the oversight. I apologize for the distress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not just distress. It's my life. I'm seventy-four years old. I can't afford mistakes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What are you doing to make sure this doesn't happen to someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are reviewing the case with the surgical team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't tell me when I'll know if I'm actually okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be checking in on you throughout the day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. I want to go home and be with Arthur.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you miss him very much.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Everyone just says they're sorry. Sorry doesn't fix the blood in my veins.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are right. My apology doesn't change the fact that the error occurred. I only hope that we can move forward with the care you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even know if I trust you anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you would feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is the next thing that happens? Exactly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the nurse come in and we'll monitor your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how you feel this evening.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and patient despite repeated pushback and emotional distress.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion', 'steps... were skipped') without explicitly naming the specific error.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language and takes full personal accountability ('I am responsible', 'I failed') without deflection.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('exhausted', 'overwhelming') and engages with the patient's shared content regarding her husband Arthur.

T.justification: The plan consists of vague steps ('keep a close eye', 'monitor your vitals') with no defined patient role.
